1503: Ithaca is Venetian. Stato da Mar: 'Ithaca: 1503-1797'. Previous holder is my reading.

region.text: Ravenna: 'Julius took Ravenna with Alfonso d'Este's help'

ledger.note: 1509: Ravenna page: 'Ravenna was then ruled by Venice until 1509, when the region was invaded in the course of the War of the League of Cambrai.' region.text: the Polesine, seized by Alfonso d'Este

ledger.note: 1509: 'd'Este seized the Polesine', won by Venice in 1484.

region.text: Padua, Verona and Vicenza, 'left undefended and surrendered to Maximilian's emissaries'

ledger.note: May 1509: after Agnadello Venice lost 'all the territory that they had accumulated in northern Italy during the previous century'; 'Padua, Verona, and Vicenza were left undefended and surrendered to Maximilian's emissaries'.

region.text: Venetian territory as far east as Brescia: Brescia, Bergamo, Crema and Cremona

ledger.note: 14 May 1509 (Agnadello): 'Louis proceeded to occupy Venetian territory as far east as Brescia without encountering any significant resistance'; the page adds that the Venetians 'lost all the territory that they had accumulated in northern Italy'. Brescia is the page's eastern limit, and Bergamo, Crema and Cremona lie west of it; the League's terms of 10 December 1508 gave them to France ('France would annex Brescia, Crema, Bergamo, and Cremona to its Milanese possessions'). The page names no city taken in May, so the three provinces are my reading of that sentence (Crema lies in Cremona province). Cliopatria's shape draws no Cremona or Crema. Replaces the bridged Cremona loss of December 1516 and the Brescia loss of February 1512 as the first loss of the Lombard Terraferma.
17 July 1509: 'Padua revolted in mid-July 1509 and returned to Venetian control on 17 July'; Maximilian lifted the siege on 1 October.
Mid-November 1509: 'Pitigliano recaptured Vicenza'.

1512, before 18 February: Brescia 'had rebelled against the French and garrisoned itself with Venetian troops' (Cambrai page). The page dates the sack, not the rebellion; the year is the page's and the rebellion's month is not given. Brescia had been French since May 1509.

18 February 1512: 'Sack of Brescia. French victory over Venice' (timeline); Gaston de Foix returned to Lombardy to sack Brescia, which 'had rebelled against the French and garrisoned itself with Venetian troops'. [Repair eu-13-c, 2026-10-31: the loss was dated February 1512 as if Brescia had been Venetian until then; it was French from May 1509 (see the 1509 loss), so this is the loss of the rebel city after its brief return.]

1514: Rovigo page: the Este 'recovered the city during the War of the League of Cambrai', and 'the Venetians, returning in 1514, retained possession until the French Revolution'. This closes the 1509 loss of the Polesine (the Cambrai page says only that d'Este 'seized the Polesine for himself'); the page names Rovigo, not the whole Polesine.

Bridging: no page opened dates the return of Bergamo and Crema (Bergamo, Crema and Brescia pages are silent on 1509-1516). The main page says 'After seven years of ruinous war, the Serenissima regained its mainland dominions west to the Adda River' (1509 + 7 = 1516), and the Cambrai page has the Treaty of Brussels (6 December 1516) confirm Venetian claims in Lombardy 'except for Cremona'. Year and counterpart are my reading.
January 1517: 'Verona surrendered to the Venetians in January 1517, when key treaty provisions took effect'; the war ended with the final truce.
January 1517: the War of the League of Cambrai ends for Venice with the return of Verona (span December 1508 to December 1516 in the lead; the final truce took effect in January 1517).

1520: Brescia page: 'The French occupied Brescia until 1520, when Venetian rule resumed.' That is the only page that dates the return. It sits uneasily with the Cambrai page, where the Treaty of Brussels (6 December 1516) 'confirmed Venetian claims to the remainder of the Imperial possessions in Lombardy (except for Cremona)', and with the main page ('Venice regained Brescia and Verona from France, also', undated); a return in 1516-1517 is therefore possible. The year is the page's (confidence 2, not 3, because the pages disagree). [Repair eu-13-c, 2026-10-31: was a bridged 1517 gain at confidence 1.]

wars.outcome: 'Venice surrendered the bases of Lepanto, Durazzo, Modon, and Coron' (main page); Venice gained Cephalonia (1500) and Ithaca (1503) per Stato da Mar.

wars.name: War of the League of Cambrai

zones.text: the Venetian mainland west of Treviso and the Romagna

wars.outcome: Agnadello (14 May 1509) cost Venice its fifteenth-century mainland; Padua (17 July) and Vicenza (November 1509) were recovered, Brescia lost in February 1512, and the treaties of Noyon (August 1516) and Brussels (6 December 1516) with Verona's return in January 1517 closed the war.

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian War (1570-1573)
wars.outcome: Nicosia fell on 9 September 1570 and Famagusta on 1 August 1571; the peace of 7 March 1573 made Cyprus an Ottoman province, with an indemnity of 300,000 ducats and a modified Dalmatian border.

wars.name: Uskok War
wars.outcome: Venice fought Archduke Ferdinand; the page gives no territorial result.
wars.note: Listed so that the reviewer sees it was considered.

wars.name: Cretan War (1645-1669)
wars.outcome: Chania fell on 22 August 1645, Rethymno on 20 October 1646, Candia on 5 September 1669; Venice kept Tinos, Kythera, Spinalonga, Gramvousa and Souda and gained ground in Dalmatia (Klis, Novigrad).
wars.note: Tenedos and Lemnos were held 1656-1657 and lost again (8 July/20 August 1656; 31 August/12 November 1657).

wars.name: Morean War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Karlowitz, January 1699: 'Morea ceded to Venice; Venetian gains in inland Dalmatia'; Venice also kept Aegina and Kephalonia and gave up Popovo polje, Klek and Sutorina.
wars.note: Venice failed at Negroponte in 1688 (siege 13 July - 22 October) and took Chios in 1694, losing it after February 1695.

wars.name: Ottoman-Venetian War (1714-1718)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans retook the Morea in 1715 'within a hundred days'; the Treaty of Passarowitz (21 July 1718): 'Morea ceded back to the Ottoman Empire; some Venetian gains in Dalmatia'.
wars.note: The Ottoman siege of Corfu (19 July - 20 August 1716) failed.

wars.name: French invasion of the Venetian state and the fall of the Republic

zones.text: Venetian territory up to the Adige

wars.outcome: French forces occupied the state up to the Adige by the end of 1796; preliminaries of 18 April 1797 gave the Balkan possessions to Austria and the Lombard part to France; Manin surrendered on 12 May; Campo Formio (17 October 1797) shared the territory.

certainty.note: The lagoon duchy's mainland extension is only 7 to 19 km (main page) and the Dalmatian, Aegean and Peloponnesian possessions are ports and islands whose limits no treaty fixed; the Treaty of Zadar of 1358 is the first dated frontier on the pages opened.

Port-and-island possessions and a mainland whose limits follow wars (Cambrai, Ferrara, Lodi); the Dalmatia line of 1358 and the lines of the 1516-1517 settlement are treaty lines but not described in the pages opened.

The Ottoman frontier is fixed by the treaties of Karlowitz (1699) and Passarowitz (1718); the Terraferma frontiers of the eighteenth century are not on a page opened here (taken as sharp by default, weak).

notes:
ONE STATE. Cliopatria's 'Republic of Venice' row (705-1796, 69 shapes, one Wikipedia article, one Wikidata id Q4948) is the continuous Venetian state from the lagoon duchy of Venetia to the fall of the republic, so it is kept as one dossier and not split; the 'spans 1091 years' flag does not apply (the doges' duchy and the republic are one state; the main page has no date for a change of constitution). The state began in 697 by tradition (726 for the first recorded doge) and ended on 12 May 1797; Cliopatria runs 705-1796, so two keyframes (697-704 and 1797) are new.

AREAS. None of the 15 pages opened gives an area in km2 (the infobox of the main page has a 2.5 million population estimate only; Stato da Mar, Domini di Terraferma and Kingdom of Candia have none), so the infobox-area comparison could not be made. Cliopatria's largest shape is 65,312 km2 (1687-1690).

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO CORRECT (all in keyframe_review): the Istrian polygon in 705-999 (Venetian Istria dates from the year 1000 on the pages); Zara drawn in 1188-1201 (Stato da Mar: lost 1186, retaken 1202); Durazzo and Corfu kept to 1240 (ended 1213 and 1214); Cephalonia and Zakynthos drawn 1210-1325 (Partitio paper allotment; Venetian only from 1500 and 1479); a Corfu polygon in 1326-1332 (Venetian 1386); the Dalmatian coast kept five years past the Treaty of Zadar (1358 against 1363); Euboea kept four years past 1470; the Messenia ports (Modon, Coron, Navarino) kept to 1506 (lost 1500-1501); Cambrai (1509-1517: the shapes keep Verona and Brescia throughout); Ulcinj kept to 1578 (lost 1571); Chania and Rethymno kept to 1647; Candia kept to 1672 (lost 1669); the Morea kept to 1717 (lost 1715). Ten new keyframes carry these (697, 1202, 1214, 1358, 1470, 1509, 1517, 1669, 1715, 1797).

CLIOPATRIA FEATURES NO PAGE OPENED EXPLAINS (unverified: page budget): a Crimean polygon at Sudak/Soldaia (34.4-35.4E, 44.8-45.1N) in 1206-1278, 1305-1374 (Stato da Mar and the Partitio page are silent on any Venetian Black Sea holding); a polygon near Kos (26.9-27.2E) in 1206-1249, 1260-1325; the central-Dalmatia dip in 1169-1187 and the Dalmatia/Kvarner dip in 1440-1449; the Euboea dip in 1279-1284; Albanian-coast polygons near Vlore in 1326-1332; a large Attica-Boeotia polygon in 1395-1406; Kythira drawn only from 1363 though Stato da Mar has it from 1238; the Aegean islands drawn from 1385 though Stato da Mar lists them from 1207 (Duchy of the Archipelago, Cliopatria 1210-1313, overlaps the same islands, so direct rule and suzerainty are not separated).

PAGES THAT DISAGREE. Rovigo: main page 1481, War of Ferrara page 17 August 1482 (the war page is used). Argos: Stato da Mar 1394-1462, Ottoman-Venetian War page 3 April 1463 (the war page is used). Gramvousa: Stato da Mar 1691, Kingdom of Candia page 'finally taken by the Turks in 1715'. Capital moved to Rivoalto: infobox 810, body text 812, History page c. 810. Pax Nicephori: 803 on the History page (812 is the usual date, not on a page opened). Zara: the main page says Venice conquered it 'the following year' after 1202, the History page and Stato da Mar say 1202. Herceg Novi: 30 September 1687 and, in the Montenegro section of the Morean War page, '31 September'. Lefkada: Stato da Mar 1684-1797 without a break, the 1714-1718 war page says the Ottomans occupied it after the Morea fell and describes no recapture. The 1714-1718 war page gives few Passarowitz terms (it does not list Tinos, Aegina, Cerigo, Butrint, Parga); the infobox line 'Morea ceded back to the Ottoman Empire; some Venetian gains in Dalmatia' is all it states. Stato da Mar's Amfissa 1687-1697 is not in the ledger.

NOT REACHED (page budget of 14; the 15th URL opened was a disambiguation page, replaced by the right article). Not opened and therefore not in the ledger: the Venetian share of Constantinople, Thrace around Adrianople, Gallipoli, the Levantine quarters (the Partitio allotment, not drawn); Thessalonica 1423-1430 (the Byzantine dossier records the hand-over of 14 September 1423 to Venice); Ravenna 1441-1509 and Crema 1449 (Crema 1429 in the Milan dossier); Tenedos 1377-1381; the Ottoman-Venetian War of 1537-1540 (only its results, from Stato da Mar: Nauplia and Monemvasia 1540, the northern Sporades 1538); Chios 1694; the Venetian Istria of the thirteenth century (the Aquileia dossier records the western Istrian coast in 1291); Dalmatia 1102-1133 (the Hungary dossier records a Venetian seizure of the Dalmatian cities in 1116 and Hungarian recovery of all but Zadar in 1133; Cliopatria and the ledger here keep Venice in Dalmatia throughout 1000-1186, which is therefore probably too generous for 1102-1133); the Treaty of Campo Formio terms beyond one sentence; the Ionian islands in 1797. RULERS omitted: no list of doges was opened (main page: 'over the centuries, 120 doges').

COUNTERPART READINGS. Where a page gives a range for a possession ('Methoni 1207-1500') but names no previous or next holder, the counterpart is my reading and the event note says so (examples: the Despotate of Epirus for Durazzo 1213, Corfu 1214 and Zakynthos 1479; the Angevin row for Corfu 1386; the Principality of Achaea for Nauplia, Argos, Patras; the Albanian principalities for Durazzo 1392, Scutari 1396, Lepanto 1407; the Ottoman Empire for the 1500 and 1503 Ionian gains). Where even a reading was too thin the counterpart reads 'holder not named by the page'. 'kingdom-of-croatia' for the year-1000 gain is also a reading.

STATES THAT NEED A DOSSIER. Republic of Saint Titus (Crete 1363-1368): written here as a rebel state from the Kingdom of Candia page alone. Scaliger rulers at Verona (lost Mestre 1337, Treviso and Bassano 1339); Carrara lordship of Padua (lost Padua and Este 1405, Carrara executed 1406); Duchy of Ferrara (the Polesine 1482-1484 and 1509); Provisional Municipality of Venice (May-October 1797). The Cliopatria rows Negroponte (1206-1209) and Duchy of the Archipelago (1210-1313) belong to another group and are Venice's vassal or neighbouring land.

SEQUENCE OF RESPONSIBILITY. The Papal States dossier (eu-13) logs a Venice contest in May 1509 for Romagna; the Duchy of Milan dossier logs Brescia 1426 and Bergamo/Crema 1429; the Patriarchate of Aquileia dossier logs the Friuli conquest in 1419-1420 with months; the Kingdom of Cyprus dossier logs 1489 February; the Hungary dossier logs 1358-02-18 and 1409/1415 Dalmatia. This dossier's events agree with those dates where the pages here give a date; the 1415 'contest_end' of the Hungary dossier has no counterpart here because the pages opened do not date the Dalmatian conquest beyond 1409 and 1420.

Applied: (1) Lombard Terraferma lost to France in May 1509 (Cambrai page: 'occupy Venetian territory as far east as Brescia'), the bridged Cremona loss of December 1516 deleted, Brescia's February 1512 loss re-read as the sack of the rebel city, Brescia's return moved to 1520 (Brescia page, which disagrees with the undated Brussels reading), Bergamo and Crema bridged to 1516 (confidence 1), Rovigo back in 1514 (Rovigo page); (2) the Cretan countryside lost in 1647 (Cretan War page) with new 1647 and 1651 keyframes; (3) the Cyclades re-coded as a vassal relation with the Duchy of the Archipelago (1418-1537, Duchy page), the direct Cyclades gain narrowed to Tinos and Mykonos, the direct losses of Syros, Naxos and the others deleted; (4) Euboea as a vassal of Venice 1209-1390 and a gain in 1390 (Triarchy page), taken out of the direct shape 1210-1389; (5) Patras lost 1430, northern Sporades gained 1453, Aegina in the Morea gain of 1699; (6) counterparts set to the neighbour dossiers (Nauplia: lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia, 12 December 1388; Argos: despotate-of-the-morea, 11 June 1394; Naupactus: despotate-of-arta; Modon and Coron: principality-of-achaea, occupied 1206 or 1207, recognised June 1209); (7) Athens: Megara 1390, Athens 18 March 1395, contest 1402, loss 1403, Boeotia taken out of the polygon; (8) Ravenna gained February 1441 (Ravenna page) and its 1509 loss confirmed; (9) thin items closed where a page was found: Thessalonica 1423-1430, western Istria 1291 and Pola 1331, Rovigo 1395-1438, Crema 1449, Lefkada 1715-1716, Dalmatia 1107-1133, and the ruler strip of 120 doges.

DISAGREEMENTS AND LEFT OPEN. Brescia: the Brescia page says 'The French occupied Brescia until 1520, when Venetian rule resumed'; the Cambrai page has the Treaty of Brussels (6 December 1516) confirm Venetian claims in Lombardy 'except for Cremona'; the main page says only 'Venice regained Brescia and Verona from France, also'. The 1520 date is the only dated sentence and is used at confidence 2; a return in 1516-1517 is possible. The Cambrai page names no city taken in May 1509: Brescia is its eastern limit and Bergamo, Crema and Cremona are the League's 1508 allotment to France (region is a reading). Cliopatria draws no Cremona, Crema, Ravenna, Thessalonica or Rovigo (before 1487) in any Venetian shape, so those events are ledger-only and the keyframes were not made to draw them; the 1509-1520 corrections subtract Cremona and Crema anyway, which removes nothing from the shape. Faenza and Rimini (1503) are on no page opened. Megara: the Nerio page says it was ceded to Venice in 1390, the Antonio I page says Carlo I Tocco sold Corinth and Megara to Theodore I in 1396; the Venetian hold was brief or nominal. Syros stays drawn in the 1385-1563 shapes as an unverified remnant (Duchy land). Lefkada: the 1714-1718 war page has the Ottomans occupy it, the Lefkada page says Venice 'abandoned' it and the Siege of Corfu page that it was 'almost immediately captured by the Ottomans'; none dates it, so 1715 is a reading (confidence 2). Doges: Anafesto and Tegalliano are not accepted as doges by modern scholars (the page). Peace of Lodi page: silent on Crema, Lodi, Piacenza; the 1447-1453 stretch (ambrosian-republic and duchy-of-milan, both confidence 1) is still a gap. Imbros, Thasos and Samothrace: the 1463-1479 war page confirms the April 1466 taking but not whether Venice kept them (the 1479 loss stays at confidence 1). Gramvousa: Stato da Mar 1691 against the Crete page 1715, unresolved. Dalmatia 1000-1107: the Croatia dossier's 1018 and 1085 losses and Venice's year-1000 gain are not reconciled here (the page has no dated sentence for 1018-1101).
